records.title: Sr. Staff Solutions Architect – Manufacturing (R6252)
records.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 

Shield AI is seeking a senior Solutions Architect – Manufacturing to serve as the functional and technical authority for Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP across Manufacturing, MRP/Supply Chain Planning, and the shop-floor-to-ERP technology stack. This role owns the design, configuration, and continuous improvement of Oracle Fusion Manufacturing and MRP capabilities, with deep, hands-on strength in MES, QMS, and PLM — ensuring plan, build, and quality processes operate as one coherent, well-architected system.

This is a hands-on, business-facing role. The Solutions Architect is expected to be the trusted advisor and go-to resource for Manufacturing and Quality business partners on any process change involving Oracle Fusion Manufacturing/Planning or the MES, QMS, and PLM bolt-on applications — translating business need into a scalable, well-architected solution, and then configuring and implementing that solution directly for medium-complexity projects. For large, complex initiatives, this person leads solution design and partners with Shield AI’s implementation partner to deliver, while remaining the accountable architect and voice of the business throughout.

Beyond core ERP, this role holds full ownership of Shield AI’s manufacturing-adjacent bolt-on application landscape — including MES, QMS, and PLM (Teamcenter) — and is responsible for how those systems integrate with Oracle Fusion ERP to form a coherent plan-to-build-to-quality operating model. This role partners closely with the other Solutions Architects for Supply Chain and Finance on shared MRP/planning signals, supplier quality matters tied to Procure-to-Pay and end-to-end integration with Finance/Accounting.



What you'll do: 




SOLUTION ARCHITECTURE & BUSINESS PARTNERSHIP

 - Designs and delivers technical solutions, creates detailed solution designs, specific integration points, and selects appropriate tools and frameworks. Collaboration with developers and engineers to implement solutions, conducts technical reviews and resolves design challenges.

 - Documents architectures, provides technical guidance during development, and ensures solutions adhere to performance, security, and interoperability requirements. Prototypes new approaches and evaluates emerging technologies for project suitability.

 - Serve as the primary point of contact and trusted advisor for business partners across Manufacturing, Production Planning, Quality, and Engineering on process design and system capability questions.

 - Act as the lead advocate for Manufacturing and Quality stakeholders in all ERP, MES, QMS, and PLM-related discussions, ensuring their operational needs, constraints, and priorities are represented in solution design.

 - Become the go-to resource for any proposed Manufacturing or Quality process change, evaluating impact, feasibility, and fit within the Oracle Fusion ERP data model and integration landscape before implementation.

 - Translate business requirements into scalable solution designs that balance standard Oracle Fusion functionality against configuration, extension, or integration needs.

 - Maintain a working command of adjacent end-to-end flows (Order-to-Cash, Procure-to-Pay) to ensure Manufacturing, MRP, MES, and QMS designs do not create downstream conflicts or gaps.


HANDS-ON CONFIGURATION & DELIVERY

 - Directly configure Oracle Fusion Manufacturing, Supply Chain Planning/MRP, Work Definitions, Quality Inspections, and related modules for medium-sized projects, enhancements, and break/fix work.

 - Build, test, and deploy configuration changes, including setup of Fusion functional areas, security, workflows, approval rules, and data structures related to manufacturing and planning processes.

 - Author functional design documents, configuration workbooks, test scripts, and process/procedure documentation to support changes made in the environment.

 - For large or highly complex initiatives, define solution architecture and requirements, then partner closely with the implementation partner to execute — remaining accountable for solution quality, business fit, and knowledge transfer.

 - Participate in and help lead workshops, fit-gap sessions, and design reviews with Manufacturing and Quality stakeholders and implementation partner teams.


MRP, MES & QMS OWNERSHIP

 - Own MRP and Supply Chain Planning configuration — planning parameters, supply/demand netting, exception messages, and planner workbench — ensuring plans translate cleanly into executable work orders.

 - Own the functional roadmap, configuration governance, and business alignment for:

–    MES (Manufacturing Execution System) — work order execution, shop-floor data collection, routing/operation tracking

–    QMS (Quality Management System) — inspections, non-conformance, corrective/preventive action (CAPA), supplier quality

–    PLM – Teamcenter — engineering BOM, item master, and change management integration with Oracle Fusion

 - Ensure MES, QMS, and PLM remain architecturally aligned with Oracle Fusion Manufacturing and MRP, avoiding duplicate data ownership, conflicting BOM/routing data, or process gaps across systems.

 - Define and maintain the target integration model between MES, QMS, PLM, and Oracle Fusion ERP, including engineering-to-manufacturing BOM transfer and quality event-to-ERP disposition flows.

 - Partner with the Solutions Architect – Supply Chain on supplier-quality data flowing from Procure-to-Pay into QMS-driven supplier corrective action processes.


INTEGRATIONS

 - Design and help implement integrations between Oracle Fusion ERP and MES, QMS, and PLM (Teamcenter), including BOM/routing sync, work order status, and quality disposition data.

 - Define integration requirements, data mappings, and error-handling/reconciliation approaches in partnership with technical/integration teams.

 - Evaluate integration patterns (API, middleware, file-based) and recommend approaches appropriate to data volume, latency, and criticality, particularly for shop-floor/real-time data.

 - Support testing, cutover, and hypercare activities for integration-related changes.


GOVERNANCE & CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT

 - Maintain configuration standards, documentation, and change control discipline for the Manufacturing, MRP, MES, QMS, and PLM functional areas.

 - Identify opportunities for process simplification, automation, and improved data quality across planning, production, and quality cycles.

 - Stay current on Oracle Fusion quarterly releases relevant to Manufacturing and Planning, and assess/recommend adoption of new features.

 - Mentor junior functional/technical resources and contribute to a growing internal ERP center of excellence.

Required Qualifications:

 - 12+ years of progressive experience in enterprise ERP systems, with significant depth in MRP/Supply Chain Planning, MES, and QMS functions.

 - Hands-on experience configuring Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP (Manufacturing and Planning pillars); comfortable working directly in the application, not solely at a requirements level.

 - Experience across multiple full-lifecycle ERP implementations (Oracle Fusion required; prior experience with Oracle EBS, SAP, or other major ERP platforms is a plus).

 - Direct, hands-on experience with at least one MES platform and one QMS platform, including their integration into an ERP environment.

 - Working knowledge of Order-to-Cash and Procure-to-Pay processes and how they interact with Manufacturing, MRP, and quality operations.

 - Demonstrated experience acting as a functional/solution architect — able to design solutions independently, not just execute configuration tasks handed down by others.

 - Experience partnering with or managing systems integrators/implementation partners on complex delivery efforts.

 - Strong business partnering and stakeholder management skills; comfortable being the primary escalation point for Manufacturing and Quality process questions.

 - Working understanding of integration concepts and experience partnering on ERP-to-MES/QMS/PLM system integrations.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience producing functional design documents, process documentation, and executive-level updates.

Preferred Qualifications:

 - Prior consulting background (Big 4, Oracle partner, or boutique Oracle Fusion implementation firm) strongly preferred.

 - Direct experience owning or integrating PLM (Teamcenter) with Oracle Fusion Manufacturing/Engineering data.

 - Experience in aerospace, defense, or other regulated/complex discrete manufacturing environments.

 - Familiarity with Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) or similar middleware/integration platforms.

 - Oracle Fusion certifications in Manufacturing, Supply Chain Planning, or Quality.

 - Experience operating in environments with export control, ITAR/CUI, or other regulated data-handling requirements.

AI & Agentic Automation Capabilities:

 - Shield AI is investing in Agentic AI to accelerate and automate manufacturing and quality operations. This role is expected to actively identify, design, and help implement AI-driven automation across Manufacturing, MRP, MES, and QMS — not simply consume AI tools built by others.
 
 - Identify high-value candidates for Agentic AI automation within Manufacturing and Quality — e.g., planner workbench exception triage, shop-floor anomaly detection, quality non-conformance routing/CAPA drafting, and work order scheduling recommendations.
 
 - Design and configure AI agent workflows using Oracle’s embedded AI/ML and agentic capabilities (e.g., Oracle Fusion AI agents, OCI Generative AI, Redwood/AI-driven planning recommendations) as they become available across Fusion Manufacturing and Planning.
 
 - Partner with IT/data teams to define prompts, guardrails, data inputs, and approval/exception paths for AI agents acting on manufacturing and quality transactions, ensuring appropriate human-in-the-loop controls.
 
 - Evaluate and pilot third-party or custom Agentic AI tools (e.g., for predictive maintenance, quality defect pattern detection, MES data synthesis, or supply/demand sensing) and assess fit against the target architecture.
 
 - Use AI-assisted tools for day-to-day solution work — requirements analysis, test script generation, configuration documentation, and data mapping — to increase delivery speed and quality.
 
 - Bring or build fluency in prompt engineering and AI workflow design; prior hands-on experience with generative AI or agentic AI platforms (Oracle AI Agent Studio, OCI Generative AI, Microsoft Copilot Studio, UiPath/Automation Anywhere agentic features, or similar) is a strong plus.
 
 - Champion responsible AI adoption — data quality, auditability, and change management — when introducing agentic workflows into regulated, ITAR/CUI-sensitive environments.

Full-time regular employee offer package:

Pay within range listed + Bonus + Benefits + Equity

 

Temporary employee offer package:

Pay within range listed above + temporary benefits package (applicable after 60 days of employment)

 

Salary compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, licenses and certifications, and specific work location. All offers are contingent on a cleared background and possible reference check. Military fellows and part-time employees are not eligible for benefits. Please speak to your talent acquisition representative for more information.

 

###

 

Shield AI is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

records.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

We are seeking a Staff Electromechanical Systems Advance Manufacturing Engineer to support the manufacturing and integration of complex motion-control and mechanically actuated systems across advanced aerospace and defense platforms. This role focuses on electromechanical assemblies involving actuators, hydraulics, pneumatics, motors, pumps, and integrated mechanical/electrical subsystems.

The ideal candidate thrives in fast-paced production environments and has experience developing robust manufacturing processes for highly integrated systems. 

What you'll do:

 - Lead manufacturing engineering efforts for electromechanical subsystems and assemblies 

 - Develop and optimize manufacturing processes, tooling, work instructions, and production flows for: 

 - Actuators 

 - Motors and drives 

 - Hydraulic systems 

 - Pneumatic systems 

 - Pumps and fluid systems 

 - Powertrain components 

 - Motion-control assemblies 

 - Partner with design engineering to improve manufacturability, reliability, testability, and producibility 

 - Drive root cause investigations and corrective actions for electromechanical manufacturing issues 

 - Develop work instructions, quality standards, and inspection methods  

 - Support supplier qualification, process validation, and production readiness reviews 

 - Lead DFM/DFA reviews and transition new products into manufacturing 

 - Support system integration, validation, and troubleshooting activities 

 - Define manufacturing standards, process controls, and acceptance criteria 

 - Support failure analysis and reliability improvement initiatives 

 - Collaborate with production, quality, supply chain, and test engineering teams 

 - Mentor junior manufacturing engineers 

Tools & skills:

 - MES & QMS systems, 3DEXPERIENCE / Teamcenter (PLM) systems, supplier manufacturing processes, 5S/visual management, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). 

Required qualifications:

 - 7+ years of manufacturing engineering experience in experience in electromechanical systems 

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechatronics, or related field 

 - Experience in prototype manufacturing in a startup or rapid-growth environment. 

 - Experience with:  

 - Actuators and motion systems  

 - Hydraulics and pneumatics  

 - Mechanical/electrical integration  

 - Precision mechanical assemblies 

 - Demonstrated ability to work in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment and adapt to changing priorities. 

 - Knowledge of manufacturing process development and production scaling  

 - Strong understanding of DFM/DFA principles  

 - Experience with root cause analysis and corrective action methodologies  

Preferred qualifications:

 - Aerospace, defense, robotics, or automotive industry experience  

 - Experience with servo systems and motor control assemblies  

 - Knowledge of GD&T and mechanical inspection methods  

 - Familiarity with lean manufacturing and production optimization 

 - Experience with ERP/MES systems and manufacturing data analysis 

 - Strong project management skills, including experience managing multiple priorities and deadlines 

 - Knowledge of quality standards, such as AS9100 or ISO 9001 

 - Proficiency in CAD software

#LD

 

Full-time regular employee offer package:

Pay within range listed + Bonus + Benefits + Equity

 

Temporary employee offer package:

Pay within range listed above + temporary benefits package (applicable after 60 days of employment)

 

Salary compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, licenses and certifications, and specific work location. All offers are contingent on a cleared background and possible reference check. Military fellows and part-time employees are not eligible for benefits. Please speak to your talent acquisition representative for more information.

 

###

 

Shield AI is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

 - Production operations  

 - Manufacturing process development  

 - DFM/DFA principles  

 - Demonstrated ability to work in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment and adapt to changing priorities. 

 - Knowledge of manufacturing process development and production scaling  

 - Strong understanding of DFM/DFA principles

 - Aerospace or defense integration experience  

 - Experience supporting autonomous systems, UAVs, or advanced mobility platforms  

 - Familiarity with low-rate initial production (LRIP) and production scaling  

 - Experience with factory integration and manufacturing line design

records.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 



Job Description

We are seeking a highly motivated engineer to support the design, development, integration, and fielding of a next-generation autonomous aircraft system. This position requires a balance of technical rigor, rapid decision-making, and hands-on engineering to efficiently transition concepts into operational capability. The ideal candidate is comfortable solving complex problems, taking ownership, working within an accelerated aircraft development environment, and is motivated by getting meaningful capability into the hands of operators quickly.

This role sits within the Manufacturing Programs organization and focuses on the front end of new aircraft and defense programs. The Staff Engineer, Advanced Manufacturing Programs will lead manufacturing strategy and planning for proposals, capture efforts, internal investment decisions, and early program development. You will work across Product Development, Manufacturing Engineering, Production, Supply Chain, Quality, Test, Facilities, Finance, and Program Management to translate aircraft concepts and program requirements into credible industrial plans. This role requires the technical depth to challenge assumptions, build defensible cost and schedule inputs, and carry manufacturing commitments from proposal through program execution.



What You’ll Do

 - Lead the manufacturing workstream for defense proposals, capture efforts, and strategic planning activities, from initial concept through final submission and customer follow-up.

 - Translate aircraft architecture, design maturity, delivery requirements, production rates, and schedule constraints into executable manufacturing and industrialization concepts.

 - Develop defensible bases of estimate for recurring labor, non-recurring engineering, headcount, tooling, equipment, facilities, production support, and manufacturing schedule inputs.

 - Build production rate, capacity, staffing, learning-curve, and ramp models; develop conceptual factory flows, station strategies, resource loading, and major milestone plans.

 - Lead rapid trade studies covering make-versus-buy decisions, vertical integration, manufacturing processes, automation, tooling strategy, factory footprint, capital investment, and surge capacity.

 - Integrate inputs from Product Development, Manufacturing Engineering, Production, Supply Chain, MP&L, Quality, Test, Facilities, Finance, and Program Management into one coherent manufacturing approach.

 - Author clear customer-facing proposal content, manufacturing plans, cost and schedule narratives, risk and opportunity assessments, and responses to formal data calls. Support proposal reviews and customer presentations as needed.

 - Establish and maintain traceable assumptions, source data, rationale, sensitivities, risks, and cross-functional approvals behind manufacturing estimates and commitments.

 - Assess manufacturing maturity and readiness from concept development through prototype, pilot, low-rate initial production, and full-rate production; identify long-lead investments and enabling decisions early.

 - Develop reusable planning models, benchmarks, proposal content, and industrial reference architectures that improve speed and consistency across future programs.

 - Support broader manufacturing strategy, including network footprint, supplier capacity, facility and capital roadmaps, production technology, and multi-program resource planning.

 - Transition awarded work into execution by converting proposal commitments and assumptions into an initial manufacturing program baseline, readiness plan, and clear ownership across the operating teams.

Required Qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, aerospace, industrial, manufacturing, or systems engineering, or a related technical field.

 - 8 or more years of relevant experience in aerospace or defense manufacturing, industrialization, operations strategy, advanced program planning, or technical proposal development.

 - Demonstrated ability to turn early, incomplete technical and program inputs into a structured manufacturing plan with explicit assumptions, risks, and decision points.

 - Experience developing bottom-up manufacturing cost, labor, capacity, tooling, equipment, facility, or production ramp estimates and documenting the basis of estimate.

 - Working knowledge of aircraft production, new product introduction, manufacturing process selection, supply chain strategy, production test, and prototype-to-rate transition.

 - Strong analytical skills and proficiency building clear, auditable models in Excel or comparable tools.

 - Ability to synthesize complex cross-functional inputs into concise written proposals, executive recommendations, and customer-facing presentations.

 - Ability to work independently, make sound decisions with imperfect information, and deliver high-quality work under accelerated proposal timelines.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Master’s degree in engineering, industrial systems, operations management, business, or a related field.

 - Experience supporting defense captures, requests for information, requests for proposals, proposal color-team reviews, or government cost and pricing submissions.

 - Experience developing manufacturing strategies for aircraft, autonomous systems, or other complex electromechanical products.

 - Familiarity with government proposal requirements, basis-of-estimate development, cost estimating relationships, and manufacturing risk and opportunity analysis.

 - Experience with industrial engineering methods such as line balancing, capacity analysis, factory layout, discrete-event simulation, or production system modeling.

 - Experience planning greenfield or brownfield production facilities, capital equipment portfolios, supplier capacity, or production surge strategies.

 - Hands-on experience taking a hardware program from prototype builds into low-rate or full-rate production.

records.description:
ARS Pharmaceuticals is a fast-growing, innovative company dedicated to transforming the treatment of severe allergic reactions with  neffy® , the first and only FDA-approved needle-free epinephrine product. If you’re motivated to make a meaningful impact, this is your opportunity to join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and inclusive culture. 



 

 This is a hands-on role that will work an onsite hybrid schedule at our San Diego corporate office in the Carmel Valley area. The Manager / Senior Manager Quality Assurance owns batch disposition and product complaint management for products made at our contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs). You will review executed batch records, drive deviations and investigations to closure, and run the complaint process end to end so that every lot released meets cGMP and regulatory requirements. This is a hands-on role working daily with CMO quality teams, Regulatory, Supply Chain, and Medical Affairs.

 ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 Batch record review and disposition 

 
 Review executed batch records, packaging records, and certificates of analysis from CMOs for accuracy, completeness, and cGMP compliance.

 Verify that deviations, OOS/OOT results, and change controls tied to each lot are closed or properly assessed before release.

 Prepare lot disposition packages and recommend release, rejection, or quarantine; act as QA approver per delegation.

 Review master batch records and specifications for new and revised products.

 Track batch release timelines and partner with Supply Chain to meet commercial and clinical supply needs.

 
 Product complaint management 

 
 Own the product complaint process: intake, triage, CMO investigation requests, trending, and closure within defined timelines.

 Assess complaints for reportability (e.g., Field Alert Reports, MDRs for combination products) with Regulatory and Pharmacovigilance.

 Lead or support root cause investigations and confirm CAPAs are effective.

 Prepare complaint trend reports for management review and Annual Product Reviews.

 
 CMO Quality Oversight 

 
 Serve as day-to-day QA contact for assigned CMOs and testing labs.

 Review and approve CMO deviations, investigations, change controls, and CAPAs affecting our products.

 Manage quality agreements and quality metrics; join business reviews and person-in-plant visits as needed.

 Support CMO audits and regulatory inspections.

 
 GMP compliance and quality systems 

 
 Maintain compliance with 21 CFR Parts 210/211, 21 CFR Part 4 (combination products), ICH Q7–Q10, and EU GMP as applicable.

 Author and revise SOPs for batch disposition and complaint handling.

 Contribute to Annual Product Reviews, recall readiness, and inspection readiness.

 Lead process improvements, and represent QA on cross-functional project teams.

 
   

 KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: 

 
 Quality judgment: makes sound, documented release and reportability decisions under time pressure.

 Partner management: holds CMOs to standards while keeping relationships productive.

 Communication: writes clear investigation summaries and explains risk to non-QA colleagues.

 Ownership: tracks open items to closure without being chased.

 Primarily office-based work with occasional travel to CMO sites, including time in GMP manufacturing areas with gowning. Occasional after-hours support for urgent complaints or release needs.

 
 EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: 

 Required 

 
 Preferred Bachelor's degree in chemistry, biology, pharmacy, engineering, or related science. An acceptable combination of education and relevant experience will also be considered

 Minimum of 6+ years of QA experience

 Hands-on batch record review and lot disposition for commercial pharmaceutical or combination products.

 Direct experience managing product complaints, deviations, and CAPAs.

 Working knowledge of cGMP (21 CFR 210/211), ICH guidelines, and FDA expectations.

 Experience overseeing CMOs or external testing labs in a virtual or outsourced model.

 Strong technical writing and attention to detail.

 
 Preferred 

 
 Drug-device combination product experience (21 CFR Part 4, 820 / QMSR).

 Sterile, nasal, or inhalation dosage form experience.

 Electronic QMS experience (e.g., Veeva Vault QualityDocs/QMS, MasterControl).

 ASQ certification (CQA, CQE, or CPGP).

 
 
 At ARS, we are proud to offer a highly competitive compensation & benefits package.  

  



 
 The full-time salary range for this posted position is $145,000 to $185,000 and may be eligible for a discretionary annual performance bonus. Actual pay rates are determined by considering multiple factors including qualifications, relevance of experience, education & credentials, subject matter expertise, and other job-related factors permitted by law. 



  
 This position is also eligible for Equity, 401k matching, and our excellent benefits package including 100% employer paid Medical, Dental & Vision for employees. View the full package here:  ARS Careers Page 

 ARS Pharmaceuticals believes in Equal Opportunity for all and is committed to ensuring all individuals, including individuals with disabilities, have an opportunity to apply for those positions that they are interested in and qualify for without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, citizenship, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic. ARS Pharmaceuticals is also committed to providing reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals so that an individual can perform their job-related duties. If you are interested in applying for an employment opportunity and require special assistance or an accommodation to apply due to a disability, please contact us at careers@ars-pharma.com 

 The position will be posted until a final candidate is selected for the requisition or the requisition has a sufficient number of applications.

records.description:
ARS Pharmaceuticals is a fast-growing, innovative company dedicated to transforming the treatment of severe allergic reactions with  neffy® , the first and only FDA-approved needle-free epinephrine product. If you’re motivated to make a meaningful impact, this is your opportunity to join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and inclusive culture. 



 

 THE OPPORTUNITY 

  

 
 The Manager / Sr. Manager, Technical Operations will play a key role in executing Technical Operations programs that support the continued development and commercial supply of neffy™. The successful candidate will combine strong technical judgment, project management, and external partner leadership in a highly collaborative environment.

 Working closely with internal stakeholders and CMOs, this role provides technical and operational leadership across the ARS outsourced manufacturing network. Responsibilities include leading Technical Operations projects, supporting formulation and process development, technology transfer, GMP manufacturing activities, and resolution of technical and operational issues. The position ensures project scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, and budgets remain aligned while proactively identifying and escalating risks to support compliant, reliable, and on-time product supply.



   ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 
 Manage cross-functional Technical Operations projects and day-to-day technical and operational interactions with assigned external partners, including scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, budgets, risks, key milestones, project meetings, action tracking, scopes of work, proposals, change orders, and CMO/vendor performance metrics and KPIs (e.g., service, quality, delivery, capacity, and right-first-time).

 Serve as a Technical Operations point of contact for assigned external manufacturing partners and work closely with CMOs and internal stakeholders to ensure execution against agreed project plans and supply requirements.

 Provide technical oversight of formulation and process development, scale-up, technology transfer, process characterization, process validation/PPQ, and continued process verification activities, as applicable.

 Plan and support clinical and commercial manufacturing campaigns in coordination with CMOs, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and other internal functions; provide on-site/person-in-plant support for key manufacturing activities as needed.

 Review manufacturing and process documentation, including master and executed batch records, protocols, reports, process performance data, vendor change controls, investigations, and annual/product reviews, for technical accuracy and process performance.

 Lead or support technical assessment and resolution of manufacturing deviations, out-of-specification or atypical results, and other process issues; contribute to root-cause analysis and appropriate corrective and preventive actions in partnership with Quality Assurance.

 Assess proposed manufacturing and process changes for technical impact and support cross-functional evaluation of quality, supply, and regulatory implications.

 Monitor and trend manufacturing and process performance data to identify emerging risks, process drift, and opportunities for continuous improvement and operational excellence.

 Support vendor selection, onboarding, and qualification activities in collaboration with Quality Assurance, Supply Chain, Procurement, and other stakeholders.

 Communicate project status, technical risks, manufacturing issues, and recommend actions clearly to Technical Operations leadership and cross-functional stakeholders; escalate significant issues to appropriate decision-makers.

 Support preparation and review of CMC information for regulatory submissions and responses to health authority questions, as required.

 Support Technical Operations process improvement, business continuity, capacity planning, and other strategic operational initiatives as assigned.

 Support commercial supply operations managed within Technical Operations, including coordination with third-party logistics (3PL) providers, distribution partners, and external manufacturing/packaging partners to maintain reliable product supply.

 Support product serialization activities, including EPCIS data exchange and operational compliance with applicable Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) requirements, working with packaging, distribution, Quality Assurance, and other partners as appropriate.

 Support clinical supply activities, including coordination with Clinical Operations and external vendors for clinical packaging, labeling, distribution, inventory/expiry management, and Interactive Response Technology/Interactive Web Response System (IRT/IWRS) activities, as applicable.

 
 KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: 

 
 Strong working knowledge of current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP), pharmaceutical manufacturing operations, and applicable quality systems and regulatory expectations.

 Demonstrated technical understanding of formulation, manufacturing processes, scale-up, technology transfer, process validation, and process performance sufficient to critically evaluate CMO data and recommendations, work effectively in cross-functional technical teams, and hold external partners accountable to commitments.

 Strong project and vendor management skills, with demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, timelines, deliverables, and external partners in a fast-paced environment.

 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate complex manufacturing or process issues, develop recommendations, and communicate the rationale for action.

 Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills with the ability to communicate effectively across functions and organizational levels, including senior management and external partners.

 Well-organized, detail-oriented, and able to identify and escalate risks while maintaining focus on execution and business priorities.

 Proficiency with Microsoft Office and project/reporting tools; experience with project management, continuous improvement, or operational excellence methodologies is a plus.

 Working knowledge of commercial and clinical supply operations relevant to Technical Operations, including 3PL interfaces, serialization/EPCIS and DSCSA requirements, and clinical IRT/IWRS processes; direct experience in one or more of these areas is preferred.

 Must be able to travel domestically and internationally up to approximately 20% to support external manufacturing partners and key project activities.

 
   EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry, chemical engineering, engineering, or a related scientific/technical discipline; an advanced degree is a plus. An acceptable combination of education and relevant experience will also be considered.

 Minimum of 5 years of relevant pharmaceutical/biotechnology experience in Technical Operations, manufacturing, process/formulation development, CMC, supply chain, or a related function.

 Experience working with external CMOs/CDMOs and supporting GMP clinical and/or commercial manufacturing is strongly preferred.

 Experience with drug-device combination products, nasal/inhalation products, sterile manufacturing, commercial product launch, or PPQ is preferred.

 Experience reviewing manufacturing batch records and process documentation and supporting technical investigations, change controls, and regulatory CMC activities is preferred.

 Experience supporting commercial distribution/3PL operations, serialization/EPCIS and DSCSA compliance, and/or clinical supply and IRT/IWRS activities is preferred.

 
 
 At ARS, we are proud to offer a highly competitive compensation & benefits package.  

  



 
 The full-time salary range for this posted position is $140,000 to $175,000 and may be eligible for a discretionary annual performance bonus. Actual pay rates are determined by considering multiple factors including qualifications, relevance of experience, education & credentials, subject matter expertise, and other job-related factors permitted by law. 



  
 This position is also eligible for Equity, 401k matching, and our excellent benefits package including 100% employer paid Medical, Dental & Vision for employees. View the full package here:  ARS Careers Page 

 ARS Pharmaceuticals believes in Equal Opportunity for all and is committed to ensuring all individuals, including individuals with disabilities, have an opportunity to apply for those positions that they are interested in and qualify for without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, citizenship, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic. ARS Pharmaceuticals is also committed to providing reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals so that an individual can perform their job-related duties. If you are interested in applying for an employment opportunity and require special assistance or an accommodation to apply due to a disability, please contact us at careers@ars-pharma.com 

 The position will be posted until a final candidate is selected for the requisition or the requisition has a sufficient number of applications.

records.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Director of Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) to join our team.

 Position Description 

 Oklo Isotopes is building scalable U.S. radioisotope production capabilities in facilities dedicated to producing essential isotopes for healthcare, space, industry, research, and defense applications. Oklo’s isotope operations include the production and processing of medically and industrially important radioisotopes using advanced radiochemical processes, hot cells, gloveboxes, and specialized nuclear facilities.

 We are seeking a Director of Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) to lead the radiochemistry and CMC organization supporting Oklo’s isotope production programs, initially focused on Lu-177 production and Am-241 and Ra-226 processing for medical, industrial, and other applications.

 The Director will lead radiochemical process development and control, technology transfer, analytical strategy, process optimization, troubleshooting, validation support, and process lifecycle management, while building and managing a multidisciplinary radiochemistry team.

 The successful candidate will develop rigorous, scalable processes from development through commissioning and routine manufacturing. The role requires deep radiochemistry and isotope-processing expertise, strong technical and team leadership, and experience in nuclear, radiological, quality, and cGMP environments.

 The Director will collaborate across Manufacturing, Facility Operations, Quality, Regulatory, Radiation Safety, Engineering, and Supply Chain to establish safe, compliant, reliable, and scalable isotope production.

 This is a on-site position located in Austin, Texas.

 Specific responsibilities may include: 

 
 Lead the CMC and radiochemistry organization for isotope process development, implementation, technical support, and lifecycle management.

 Lead Lu-177 production and Am-241 and Ra-226 processing, including dissolution, separation, purification, recovery, impurity control, characterization, and waste minimization.

 Establish the technical basis for manufacturing processes, including process flows, material balances, critical parameters, operating ranges, specifications, and controls.

 Lead development, scale-up, optimization, and implementation of radiochemical processes in hot cells, gloveboxes, and laboratory or remote systems.

 Lead technology transfer and manufacturing readiness, including processes, equipment, analytics, procedures, training, and documentation.

 Establish and maintain the cGMP technical framework, including process characterization, validation, continued verification, change control, deviations, investigations, and continuous improvement.

 Own the analytical strategy for products, intermediates, impurities, waste streams, and process performance.

 Serve as the senior technical authority for process troubleshooting and optimization, focused on yield, purity, recovery, reliability, cycle time, waste, dose, and capacity.

 Support equipment design, commissioning, qualification, startup, and operational readiness with Manufacturing, Operations, Engineering, Quality, Radiation Safety, Regulatory, and Supply Chain.

 Build, mentor, and manage the radiochemistry team; establish technical standards, procedures, training, and documentation; and promote safety, quality, rigor, and operational excellence.

 Support regulatory activities, audits, inspections, and development of new isotope products, processes, technologies, and capabilities.

 
 Minimum Qualifications: 

 
 Masters in Radiochemistry, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or a closely related technical discipline.

 10+ years of progressively responsible experience in radiochemistry, isotope production, radiochemical processing, nuclear chemical operations, pharmaceutical/radiopharmaceutical manufacturing, or a closely related field.

 Experience with cGMP manufacturing (US and EU requirements), particularly radiopharmaceuticals, medical isotopes, APIs, radioactive starting materials, or other regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing.

 Experience with CMC development, process characterization, technology transfer, process validation, continued process verification, and manufacturing science and technology (MS&T).

 Direct experience with Lu-177 production, lanthanide separations, target dissolution, radionuclide purification, or medical-isotope manufacturing.

 Demonstrated experience leading technical teams responsible for complex chemical, radiochemical, or manufacturing processes.

 Strong technical background in radiochemical separations, purification, radioactive-material handling, analytical chemistry, and process development.

 Demonstrated experience translating laboratory or development processes into reliable manufacturing operations.

 Experience with process development, scale-up, process optimization, technology transfer, troubleshooting, and technical lifecycle management.

 Experience working in highly regulated environments requiring disciplined procedures, documentation, configuration control, and quality systems.

 Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical investigations and make sound decisions using scientific and engineering data.

 Experience developing technical procedures, specifications, reports, process documentation, and training materials.

 Strong leadership, communication, technical writing, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

 Demonstrated ability to collaborate across Manufacturing, Operations, Engineering, Quality, Regulatory, Radiation Safety, and other multidisciplinary organizations.

 Experience with various regulatory regimes affecting isotope production and processing (FDA, NRC, DOE, etc.) regulatory frameworks relevant to radioactive-material and isotope manufacturing.

 
 Bonus Qualifications: 

 
 Passionate about unleashing beneficial isotopes and building domestic isotope-production capabilities.

 A strong technical leader who can maintain scientific rigor while moving programs rapidly toward manufacturing.

 Committed to nuclear safety culture, product quality, procedural compliance, and operational excellence.

 Capable of moving comfortably between detailed radiochemical problems and broader program and organizational decisions.

 Able to develop people and build a high-performing technical organization.

 Comfortable making decisions in technically complex environments where complete information may not always be available.

 Effective at translating scientific development into practical, repeatable manufacturing processes.

 Collaborative and able to work across Manufacturing, Facility Operations, Quality, Regulatory, Engineering, Radiation Safety, and Supply Chain.

 Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment.

 Willing to challenge established approaches and develop novel solutions to difficult isotope-production problems.

 An excellent technical communicator capable of communicating complex chemistry and manufacturing issues clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.

 Detail-oriented and disciplined about technical documentation, configuration control, quality, and follow-through.

 Able to balance near-term production needs with long-term process robustness and manufacturing scalability.

 
 Who you are: 

 A startup person : You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

 Motivated : You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

 A team-player : Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

 An excellent communicator : We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

 Creative : Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

 Detail-oriented : This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

  

 About Oklo travel requirements: 

 Oklo requires remote employees to travel to headquarters (Santa Clara, CA) twice a quarter annually, based on business or team needs, including attendance at team meetings, off-sites, and other company events or gatherings. For the first two weeks of onboarding, employees are required to be in person at headquarters in Santa Clara, CA.

  

 About Oklo compensation: 

 Salary: $170,000-$250,000

 Oklo offers flexible time off, equity, bonuses, competitive pay, 401(k), health insurance (with employer contribution), HSA, FSA, flexible work hours, wellness credits, and other benefits.

 This position may involve access to information subject to U.S. export control laws. Only applicants who meet the definition of a U.S. person under applicable laws may be eligible.

 
 About Oklo Inc.: Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories.

 #CHOP: Oklo’s Values 
 Collaboration : We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes.
 Humility : We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition.
 Ownership : We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through  to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy.
 Pathfinding : We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity.
 Candidates should be aware that employment may be contingent upon successful completion of a drug screening, and employees may be subject to drug testing at any time in accordance with company policy and applicable laws. 

 Recruitment Fraud Disclaimer 

 Oklo is aware of recent recruitment fraud attempts targeting job seekers. Please be cautious of anyone claiming to represent Oklo who does not contact you from an official Oklo email address. 

 All legitimate communications from our recruiting team— including application updates, interview requests, and job offers — will come exclusively from an @oklo.com email. Oklo will never ask for sensitive personal information, payments, or account credentials during the hiring process. 

 If you receive suspicious outreach or have concerns about the authenticity of any communication claiming to be from Oklo, please contact us through the official channels listed on our website.

records.description:
Thank you for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Plant Manager to join our team.

 This position will be on-site at the Aurora facility at Idaho National Laboratory in Idaho. 

 Position Description 

 Oklo is developing its Aurora powerhouse at Idaho National Laboratory. The Plant Manager will coordinate the people, infrastructure, work processes, and site interfaces needed to support safe and effective facility readiness and operations.

 The Plant Manager is responsible for day-to-day facility operations and the safe, reliable, and efficient execution of maintenance, work control, logistics, and administrative activities. The manager coordinates with accountable program owners for industrial and nuclear safety, radiation protection, security, environmental requirements, and emergency preparedness. This role provides leadership across multidisciplinary teams working in a highly regulated environment.

 The Plant Manager will oversee facility readiness, site infrastructure, maintenance coordination, contractor activities, logistics, and facility support functions. The role will establish practical processes, resolve site issues, support readiness, and improve facility performance as the Aurora program advances.

 The Plant Manager will work closely with Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, Radiation Protection, Safety, Security, Emergency Preparedness, Quality, site services, contractors, program leadership, and Idaho National Laboratory organizations.

 Specific responsibilities may include: 

 
 Lead and coordinate day-to-day on-site facility operations in accordance with approved procedures, site requirements, and applicable regulatory expectations.

 Oversee facility support activities, including maintenance coordination, work control, planning and scheduling, facility readiness, logistics, material handling, and site access needs.

 Coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance, equipment issue resolution, work prioritization, and restoration of facility systems and infrastructure.

 Implement and improve facility operations programs, work-control practices, operational procedures, and performance standards.

 Coordinate facility modifications, equipment installations, infrastructure improvements, utility and support-system work, facility turnover, and related contractor activities.

 Oversee contractors, vendors, and cross-functional work teams to support safe, timely, and effective execution of on-site work.

 Support industrial and nuclear safety, radiation protection, security and access control, environmental requirements, emergency preparedness, and response to abnormal or emergent facility conditions.

 Support facility and organizational readiness activities, including assessments, action tracking, procedure implementation, staffing coordination, and transition to routine operations.

 Coordinate material receipt, storage, inventory accountability, equipment staging, deliveries, and other site logistics activities.

 Maintain facility records, logs, procedures, work-tracking systems, schedules, performance measures, and programmatic reporting.

 Support inspections, assessments, audits, corrective actions, and follow-up activities related to facility operations and site commitments.

 Coordinate with Idaho National Laboratory site services and applicable oversight interfaces to communicate facility needs, resolve issues, and track required actions.

 Promote operational discipline, procedural compliance, safety culture, accountability, and continuous improvement across facility activities.

 
 Minimum Qualifications: 

 
 Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Industrial Technology, Nuclear Engineering, or a related technical discipline; equivalent operational experience may be considered.

 Minimum of 10 years of experience supporting nuclear facility operations.

 Experience leading or coordinating multidisciplinary operational and facility-support activities.

 Demonstrated understanding of operational safety, facility maintenance coordination, work control, planning and scheduling, and procedural compliance.

 Experience coordinating contractors, site logistics, infrastructure work, or facility support services.

 Strong understanding of plant and site operations and the interfaces among Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Safety, Security, Quality, and support organizations.

 Experience working with operational procedures, work-control systems, facility records, and action-tracking processes.

 Strong organizational, leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in an on-site operational environment.

 
 Bonus Qualifications: 

 
 Previous experience supporting nuclear energy facilities, U.S. Department of Energy sites, power-generation facilities, advanced reactor projects, or other high-hazard regulated environments.

 Experience with facility turnover, startup preparation, readiness assessments, or transition to routine operations.

 Experience overseeing facility upgrades, contractor execution, infrastructure improvements, or site-services coordination.

 Experience with industrial or nuclear safety programs, radiation protection, security, emergency preparedness, environmental compliance, or quality assurance.

 Experience with computerized maintenance management, work-control, scheduling, or facility performance systems.

 Project management or facility-operations leadership experience.

 Former NRC licensed SRO.

 Former Shift Manager.

 Multi-department leadership experience.

 
 Competencies 

 We are looking for a Plant Manager who is:

 
 Passionate about clean energy and making advanced fission a reality.

 Committed to operational excellence, industrial safety, nuclear safety, and a strong safety culture.

 Willing and able to learn quickly.

 Eager to work on a dynamic team, receive constructive feedback, and grow with us.

 Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment.

 Able to lead cross-functional facility activities and coordinate competing priorities.

 Detail-oriented and committed to procedural compliance, effective work control, and operational discipline.

 Able to think creatively, critically, and reflectively about facility and operational challenges.

 Willing to propose practical solutions to technical and operational problems.

 An excellent communicator who can clearly communicate technical content, operational priorities, and facility needs.

 Capable of exercising sound judgment and making timely decisions in an on-site operational environment.

 
 Who you are: 

 A startup person : You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

 Motivated : You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

 A team-player : Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

 An excellent communicator : We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

 Creative : Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

 Detail-oriented : This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

  

 About Oklo travel requirements: 

 Oklo requires remote employees to travel to headquarters (Santa Clara, CA) twice a quarter annually, based on business or team needs, including attendance at team meetings, off-sites, and other company events or gatherings. For the first two weeks of onboarding, employees are required to be in person at headquarters in Santa Clara, CA.

  

 About Oklo compensation: 

 Salary: $180,000-$210,000 

 Oklo offers flexible time off, equity, bonuses, competitive pay, 401(k), health insurance (with employer contribution), HSA, FSA, flexible work hours, wellness credits, and other benefits.

 This position may involve access to information subject to U.S. export control laws. Only applicants who meet the definition of a U.S. person under applicable laws may be eligible.

 
 About Oklo Inc.: Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories.

 #CHOP: Oklo’s Values 
 Collaboration : We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes.
 Humility : We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition.
 Ownership : We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through  to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy.
 Pathfinding : We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity.
 Candidates should be aware that employment may be contingent upon successful completion of a drug screening, and employees may be subject to drug testing at any time in accordance with company policy and applicable laws. 

 Recruitment Fraud Disclaimer 

 Oklo is aware of recent recruitment fraud attempts targeting job seekers. Please be cautious of anyone claiming to represent Oklo who does not contact you from an official Oklo email address. 

 All legitimate communications from our recruiting team— including application updates, interview requests, and job offers — will come exclusively from an @oklo.com email. Oklo will never ask for sensitive personal information, payments, or account credentials during the hiring process. 

 If you receive suspicious outreach or have concerns about the authenticity of any communication claiming to be from Oklo, please contact us through the official channels listed on our website.

records.title: Director of Site Operations
records.description:
About the Company 

 We are a renewable energy and ocean technology company committed to rapidly developing and deploying technologies that will ensure a sustainable future for Earth by unlocking the vast energy potential of its oceans. Our focus is on capturing civilizational levels of ultra-low-cost renewable energy for applications including computing and affordable renewable fuels delivered to shore.

 The company is a public benefit corporation headquartered in Portland, Oregon, and backed by leading venture capitalists, philanthropic investors, university endowments, and private investment offices. We operate as an idea meritocracy in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis.

 Our staff have worked at organizations such as SpaceX, Blue Origin, Boeing, Tesla, Apple, Virgin Orbit, Astra, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, New Relic, Bridgewater, Raytheon, Disney Imagineering, and the US Army and Air Force, as well as research universities, startups, and small companies across a range of industries.

 About the Job 

 Our core technology is the node, a device that produces energy in the ocean’s harshest conditions for years at a time without human maintenance or intervention.

 We are seeking a Director of Site Operations to lead the day-to-day operational performance of Panthalassa’s regional facilities and build the systems that will support their growth. The Director will have direct responsibility for our headquarter and R&D campus, our Portland headquarters and primary hub for R&D, engineering, prototyping, and business operations, while leading Site Operations Managers at our other locations. Each site should have clear operational ownership, consistent support, and a leader who understands what is happening on the ground.

 You will set and sustain a high standard for how our sites are maintained, organized, and made ready for work. You will make sure that standard is reflected in daily conditions and practices across locations, and that site leaders address issues promptly and consistently. You will use sound judgment when site conditions or practices create safety, reliability, or operational concerns, working with the relevant functional leaders to resolve them and prevent recurrence.

 You will build the operating model behind that performance: clear roles and decision paths, useful site routines, responsive services, effective vendor relationships, and ways to identify and resolve recurring problems. You will keep a close view of site needs and emerging constraints, then turn what you learn into practical improvements that make operations more consistent and responsive as Panthalassa grows.

 This role connects functional expertise to local execution. You will work closely with Facilities Engineering, Workplace Experience, EHS, Security, Real Estate, IT, Capital Delivery, Manufacturing, R&D, and other teams to understand upcoming needs, coordinate work that affects a site, and ensure local priorities and constraints are addressed. Those teams retain ownership of their technical and professional standards; Site Operations ensures their work comes together effectively at each location.

 This is a systems-building and leadership role. You will remain closely involved in Banfield while building and developing Site Operations Managers who can lead their locations with clear accountability. Your success will show in sites that are consistently well-run, responsive to the people who use them, and ready to support Panthalassa’s changing work.

 Candidates should have strong interpersonal skills and be able to thrive in a creative, scrappy, and collaborative environment in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis.

 Responsibilities 

 Regional Site Operations Leadership 

 
 Lead Site Operations across Panthalassa’s regional facilities, with direct responsibility for the corporate campus and leader and mentorship of Site Operations Managers at other locations.

 Hire, develop, and manage a high-performing Site Operations team with clear ownership, priorities, and expectations.

 Establish consistent operating standards, service levels, and expectations across sites while accounting for the unique needs of each location.

 Maintain visibility into major activities, constraints, and risks across the regional portfolio and ensure resources are aligned with business priorities.

 Serve as the escalation point for significant site issues, operational conflicts, and service gaps.

 Maintain hands-on involvement at the main corporate campus facilities while developing a regional operating model that does not depend on the Director personally solving every problem.

 
 Cross-Functional Operations & Planning 

 
 Serve as a senior operational partner to Engineering, Manufacturing, R&D, Facilities Engineering, EHS, Security, IT, Real Estate, and other functions.

 Build strong relationships with functional leaders to understand upcoming work, growth plans, and operational requirements.

 Ensure Site Operations Managers are coordinating activities, shared resources, projects, moves, outages, deliveries, and other work that may affect multiple teams.

 Identify operational impacts and resource constraints before they affect execution and bring together the appropriate teams to resolve them.

 Translate company growth and changing operational requirements into site capabilities, staffing, services, and infrastructure needs.

 
 Systems & Operational Excellence 

 
 Build scalable systems, processes, and operating standards that make Panthalassa facilities high-performing, consistent, and turnkey.

 Develop common operating rhythms, escalation paths, service models, and KPIs across sites.

 Identify recurring operational friction and drive solutions that address root causes rather than repeated one-off fixes.

 Implement tools, automation, vendors, and processes that improve visibility, coordination, service quality, and efficiency.

 Establish mechanisms for sharing best practices and lessons learned between sites.

 Continuously evaluate whether current operating systems can support the next stage of company growth and evolve them before they become constraints.

 
 Site Services, Vendors & Resources 

 
 Own the strategy for the vendors and services that support site operations, including janitorial, PPE, uniforms/laundry, furniture, waste, workplace supplies, fleet, logistics, and other shared services.

 Establish regional vendor strategies and standards while supporting Site Operations Managers in local execution.

 Develop scalable inventory, procurement, and replenishment strategies for operational supplies and shared resources.

 Ensure workplace readiness along with Workplace Experience on space planning, employee accommodations, furniture, and team moves.

 Partner with EHS, Security, Facilities Engineering, Real Estate, and property management on safety, security, utilities, wastewater, landlord, and other site requirements.

 
 Budget, Team & Growth Planning 

 
 Develop and own the regional Site Operations budget, including annual planning, forecasting, and ongoing management.

 Establish site-level budgets and accountability while maintaining visibility into regional spending and future requirements.

 Build business cases for staffing, vendors, tools, services, and operational investments.

 Develop staffing and service models that scale with headcount, facility growth, and increasing operational complexity.

 Identify opportunities to improve cost and operational efficiency without compromising safety, reliability, service quality, or employee productivity.

 
 Required Qualifications 

 
 8+ years of experience in site operations, facilities operations, industrial operations, workplace operations, or a related field, including experience leading teams.

 Experience supporting industrial, engineering, manufacturing, laboratory, R&D, or similarly complex environments.

 Demonstrated ability to build and scale operational systems, teams, processes, and service models.

 Experience managing operations across multiple facilities, sites, or complex operating environments.

 Strong systems thinking and the ability to understand how people, facilities, services, resources, and business activities interact.

 Experience managing significant operating budgets, vendors, procurement, and operational services.

 Strong people leadership with experience developing managers and building effective teams.

 Excellent cross-functional communication and the ability to influence and coordinate across technical and operational organizations.

 Strong judgment with the ability to balance immediate operational needs against long-term scalability.

 Comfortable operating at both strategic and tactical levels in a fast-changing environment.

 
 Desired Qualifications 

 
 Experience in a fast-growing startup or scale-up environment.

 Experience building a regional or multi-site operations function.

 Experience supporting headquarters, R&D campuses, manufacturing facilities, or mixed office/industrial environments.

 Familiarity with industrial safety and commercial building operations.

 Experience developing operational KPIs, service standards, and vendor strategies across multiple sites.

 Experience supporting significant facility growth, new site launches, or organizational scaling.

 
 The above qualifications are desired, not required. We encourage you to apply if you are a strong candidate with only some of the desired skills and experience listed.

 Additional Requirements 

 
 This is an on-site leadership role based primarily at the main corporate campus.

 Regular travel between Panthalassa’s regional locations is required.

 Ability to move regularly throughout office, lab, shop, and industrial environments.

 Intermittent availability outside normal business hours may be required for significant site issues or operational needs.

 Travel to vendors and test sites as needed

 Intermittently able to work longer hours and weekends to support critical needs. While we expect a lot of each other, we also offer a high degree of autonomy and work-life balance, including flexible PTO and flexible working hours.

 
 Compensation and Benefits 

 If hired for this full-time role, you will receive:

 
 Cash compensation of $190,000–$225,000.

 Equity in the company. We’re all owners and if we’re successful, this equity should be far and away the most valuable component of your compensation.

 A benefits package that helps you take care of yourself and your family, including:
 
 Flexible paid time off

 Health insurance (the company pays 100% of gold-level PPO plan for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents)

 Dental insurance (the company pays 100% for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents)

 Vision insurance (the company pays 100% for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents)

 Disability insurance (the company pays 100% for a policy to provide long-term financial support if you become disabled)

 Ability to contribute to tax-advantaged accounts, including 401(k), health FSA, and dependent care FSA

 


 Relocation assistance to facilitate your move to Portland (if needed).

 
 Location 

 This is an on-site position. Our offices, lab, and shop are located in Portland, Oregon.
